verdict.rationale: vLLM's docs list integer quantization formats (INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF) and say quantization trades precision for a smaller memory footprint, so the 4-bit to 8-bit range is covered. The 'very low-bit' end of the story (below 4-bit, e.g. 2–3 bit) is not explicitly documented. An early community comment said 4-bit was unsupported, but current docs list INT4, so it is not a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: explicit documentation of sub-4-bit integer quantization, independent hands-on corroboration of memory savings across the INT range

support.subject: As a power-user, I can reduce memory footprint using integer quantization ranging from very low-bit to 8-bit precision

citations.quote: Quantization: FP8, MXFP8/MXFP4, NVFP4, INT8, INT4, GPTQ/AWQ, GGUF, compressed-tensors, ModelOpt, TorchAO, and more
